title: Properties of a water-main plan

blocks.text: A water utility selects which mains to replace this year, and its selection code is about to be rewritten. Before the rewrite, the team wants property-based tests that would notice if the new code broke a business rule. You write the three properties; the tests run them under Hypothesis.

An instance has projects $`P`$, each with a capital cost $`a_p`$ and an operating cost $`o_p`$, a capital budget $`A`$ and an operating budget $`O`$, must-do projects $`M \subseteq P`$, and for each project a set $`N_p`$ of prerequisites, projects that must be funded whenever $`p`$ is. The selection, with $`y_p \in \{0, 1\}`$ and $`v_p`$ the project's value, is

\begin{aligned}
\max\ & \sum_{p \in P} v_p\, y_p \\
\text{s.t. } & \sum_{p} a_p\, y_p \le A && \text{(capital)} \\
& \sum_{p} o_p\, y_p \le O && \text{(operating)} \\
& y_p = 1 && \forall p \in M \quad \text{(must}_p) \\
& y_p \le y_q && \forall p \in P,\ q \in N_p \quad \text{(needs}_{p,q})
\end{aligned}

The docstring of `water_properties.py` gives the instance's dict shape; a plan is the set of funded projects. Write the three functions. Each returns `None` when its property holds for the plan and fails an `assert` when it does not:

items: `within_both_budgets`: the plan's spend fits both budgets;
`must_dos_funded`: every must-do is in the plan;
`prerequisites_funded`: no funded project lacks any of its prerequisites.

blocks.text: Check the plan against the instance's data, not against a solver. The tests draw instances that are feasible by construction and run each property, as the body of a Hypothesis test, on the plans of a correct solver (it must hold on every one) and of solvers that break a rule (it must fail on some). Ties between equal plans do not matter. About eight lines.

cases.says: the budget property holds on every plan of the correct solver and fails on a solver that ignores both budgets
the must-do property holds on the correct solver and fails on one that treats must-dos as optional
the prerequisite property holds on the correct solver and fails on one that ignores prerequisites
a solver that keeps to the capital budget but ignores the operating one is caught
a project with two prerequisites needs both, so a solver satisfied by one of them is caught

origin.section: Validity Properties Miss a Rule That Is Too Strict; a Witness Catches It

concepts: a property states a business rule and checks each returned plan against the data, not against the model
a property earns its place by failing on code that breaks its rule
